stem: The graph of the quadratic function \(y = f(x)\) is shown in the \(xy\)-plane. For which of the following values of \(x\) is \(f(x) > 0\)?
solution: \(f(x) > 0\) where the graph is above the \(x\)-axis.
The graph crosses the \(x\)-axis at \(x = -2\) and \(x = 4\) and is above the axis between these crossings, since the parabola opens downward.

explanation.A: Correct. Between the \(x\)-intercepts \(-2\) and \(4\) the graph is above the \(x\)-axis.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Outside the intercepts the graph is below the \(x\)-axis, so \(f(x) < 0\) there.
explanation.C: Incorrect. \(0\) and \(9\) are \(y\)-values (the graph reaches up to \(9\)), not the \(x\)-values where the graph crosses the axis.
explanation.D: Incorrect. \(x = 1\) is where the maximum occurs, but \(f(x)\) is positive on both sides of it, up to \(x = 4\) only.

verify:
x = symbols('x')
f = sympify(figure['curves'][0]['expr'])
assert sorted(solve(f, x)) == [-2, 4] and Poly(f, x).LC() < 0
assert choices[answer] == r'\(-2 < x < 4\)'
assert all(p['y'] != 0 for p in figure['points'])
